headline: Glitter for eternity: Country singer Dolly Parton has died. An obituary
lead: Dolly Parton, who turned artificiality into an art form and self-irony into a kind of sovereignty, dies at 80. Her songs transcended the boundaries between tradition and pop.
seo_title: US country singer Dolly Parton has died. She was 80 years old
social_title: US country singer Dolly Parton has died. She was 80 years old
print_title: US country singer Dolly Parton has died. She was 80 years old
print_subtitle: US country singer Dolly Parton has died. She was 80 years old
summary_bullets_en: Country singer Dolly Parton has passed away at the age of 80 in Nashville.
She wrote approximately 3,000 songs, including hits like "Jolene," won 11 Grammys, and sold over 100 million records.
She left a lasting legacy with her Dollywood theme park and children's Imagination Library.

original_de.headline: Glitzer für die Ewigkeit: Die Country-Sängerin Dolly Parton ist gestorben. Ein Nachruf
original_de.lead: Dolly Parton machte aus Künstlichkeit eine Kunst und aus Selbstironie eine Form der Souveränität. Mit ihren Songs überwand sie die Grenzen zwischen Tradition und Pop. Nun ist sie im Alter von 80 Jahren gestorben.

body.caption: Dolly Parton in a recording from 1970.

body.text: What was Dolly Parton's most famous line? A lyric from one of her global hits, perhaps «I Will Always Love You»? Or that self-description she coquettishly carried through almost every interview: «I'm just a simple, silly country girl»? It was probably a line about her body: «It costs a lot to look this cheap.» Anyone who wanted to mock her enormous hair, artificial fingernails, or bust was always a little too late. Parton had already made a joke about it herself.

The singer found that she had not invested millions in cosmetic surgery for it to be deliberately overlooked afterwards. Thanks to such remarks, her popularity remained consistently high for decades. Soprano voice, seductive power and self-irony – no one mastered this combination better.
Provincial roots and glamour

Indeed, the woman who has been considered the quintessential female country icon since the 1960s can also be seen from today's perspective as an avant-gardist of artistic self-staging. Parton's influence continues to be felt in the carefully curated images of contemporary pop princesses: exaggerated femininity, a keen instinct for marketing her own persona – and the knowledge that artificiality and artistic authenticity are by no means mutually exclusive.

The wigs and nails never obscured her musical genius. She wrote timeless country, gospel and bluegrass songs. And she sang with a voice that made even the most down-to-earth subjects sound weightless.

Dolly Parton bridged various divides. Who before her had managed to evoke a sensibility that oscillated between truck stop and gay bar, honky-tonk and Hollywood? This combination of country and pop, provincial roots and glamour, was later also found in the songs of her goddaughter Miley Cyrus. Especially after Parton's appearance in Miley Cyrus's series «Hannah Montana» and collaborations with younger pop singers like Kesha, a new generation discovered Parton's charm. She was never considered old news; that was for others.

body.caption: Dolly Parton sang with a voice that made even the most down-to-earth subjects sound weightless. Image: 2014.

body.text: Church performances

Dolly Parton had an impoverished childhood. The doctor who delivered her on Jan. 19, 1946, in Sevier County, Tennessee, the fourth of twelve children, was reportedly paid with a sack of cornmeal. The sharecropper family's one-room cabin at the foot of the Great Smoky Mountains was as far removed as imaginable from the glittering world Parton would later create. There was no running water, and music was only to be found in her grandfather's church.

Dolly Parton performed in church services starting at age six. She learned to play guitar, banjo, piano and the Appalachian dulcimer. By age ten, she was a regular on local radio and television stations. When she performed at the legendary Grand Ole Opry in Nashville at age thirteen, she met Johnny Cash. He took the young singer aside and told her to always follow her own instincts.

body.caption: Dolly Parton at the age of nine. Although her family was poor, she said that imagination was more important to her than possessions.

body.text: Outwardly, Dolly Parton may have modeled herself on a somewhat overambitious beauty queen – but her music felt real and honest. Her clear, almost ethereal voice sometimes also spoke of a vulnerable, long-suffering, or even insecure self. In «Coat of Many Colors,» she sings about the ridicule she endured as a child because of her coat sewn from fabric scraps. The classic «Jolene» deals with a humiliation: her husband's flirtation with a stranger.

Dolly Parton achieved her first successes less as a singer than a songwriter. She wrote hits for Bill Phillips and Skeeter Davis, for Hank Williams Jr. and Kitty Wells. Her breakthrough as a singer came in 1967 when country star Porter Wagoner made her a regular on his television show. Their first duet together, «The Last Thing on My Mind», was already a success. For six years, Parton and Wagoner were fixtures on the country charts. Then Parton dissolved the partnership, which was increasingly strained by resentment.

She did, however, write a farewell anthem for her musical ex-partner: «I Will Always Love You.» The song became one of her biggest hits. Elvis Presley wanted to record it – but his manager Tom Parker demanded half of the publishing rights. Parton refused. Today, many know the song primarily through Whitney Houston's version, which she recorded in 1992 for the film «The Bodyguard» and turned into a global hit.

The separation from Wagoner opened the door to Hollywood for Dolly Parton. Alongside Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin, she starred in the hit comedy «9 to 5.» The plot – three women who united against their selfish, sexist and authoritarian boss – almost incidentally turned the country diva into a feminist icon. The title song she wrote did the rest, conquering both the pop and country charts.

body.caption: Dolly Parton (center) with actresses Lily Tomlin (left) and Jane Fonda (right) in the comedy «Nine to Five».

body.text: However, the artist never allowed herself to be pigeonholed – neither musically nor socio-politically. When younger country musicians adopted her successful blend of country and pop in the 1990s, she returned to her own roots. A series of bluegrass-inspired albums opened up a new audience to her: the young alternative country scene.
Openness, not naiveté

Dolly Parton claimed to wear her heart on her sleeve on stage. However, this openness should not be mistaken for naiveté. She controlled her image with the utmost professionalism and a keen sense of how diverse her audience was.

She catered to the conservative country audience with gospel songs and Great Smoky Mountains folklore. In turn, she reached the gay community with her flamboyant, playfully exaggerated femininity. And Parton even found a way to connect with the hip-hop generation: in «Joyful Noise,» she played the widow of a choir director alongside rapper Queen Latifah.

She had bravely fought «a short battle» against cancer and died in a cancer center surrounded by her relatives, her team announced Tuesday evening local time in a statement provided to American media.
For six decades, Dolly Parton wrote, sang, acted and produced, tirelessly and with a work ethic that she gladly hid behind the glitter. Dolly Parton died on Aug. 25, 2026, at the age of 80.

Parton's fans mourn her worldwide. Bouquets of flowers were laid on her star plaque on Hollywood's «Walk of Fame.» Pop star Elton John honored her as a «gigantic artist» with the «kindest heart.» Oscar winner Jane Fonda called Parton «so present, so strong, so generous and playful that she is forever woven into our lives and hearts.» President Donald Trump ordered flags across the country to be flown at half-mast for a week. In honor of the deceased artist, the Empire State Building in New York illuminated its spire in glittering pink light that evening.

body.caption: Flowers lie on Dolly Parton's star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.
